class.name: CgameFFTOcean

method.name: displacement_image
method.description: Evaluates the heights at [param time] and returns them as a single-channel [constant Image.FORMAT_RF] image of size [member n] by [member n] for a displacement shader.

method.name: evaluate
method.description: Returns [code]n * n[/code] heights (row-major) at [param time] in seconds. Updates [member last_max_imag]. Returns an empty array if [method setup] was not called.

method.name: fft_1d
method.description: Applies a radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT to the complex signal given by the real parts [param re] and imaginary parts [param im] and returns the result as the array [code][re, im][/code]. The forward transform uses [code]e^(-i...)[/code]; the inverse uses [code]e^(+i...)[/code] and scales by [code]1/N[/code], so the inverse of the forward transform restores the input. The size must be a power of two and both arrays must have the same size. [b]Note:[/b] Unlike the GDScript version, which modifies the arrays in place, packed arrays are passed by value to native methods, so the transformed data is returned instead.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: Returns the bilinearly interpolated height at [param position] (meters, x and z of the ocean surface) from a grid previously returned by [method evaluate]. The grid tiles with period [member patch_size], so any position is valid.

method.name: setup
method.description: Builds the Phillips spectrum deterministically. [param grid] is the number of samples per side and must be a power of two of at least 4. [param patch] is the side length of the simulated square in meters, [param wind] gives the wind direction and speed in meters per second, [param amplitude] scales the wave height, and [param seed] seeds the random number generator.

members.member: The largest absolute imaginary part seen by the last [method evaluate]. It should be close to zero for a real field.
Number of samples per side of the height grid. Set through [method setup].
Side length of the simulated patch in meters. Set through [method setup].
